__inputs.name: DS_TRINO
__inputs.label: Trino
__inputs.description: Trino datasource of the platform (for system.runtime tables)

description: Trino cluster (Stackable operator): query throughput, latency and failures, per-phase timing from the query TIMELINE logs, coordinator query history (system.runtime.queries), cluster memory, tasks/splits, JDBC connector (PostgreSQL catalogs), JVM/pod resources and logs. Metrics come from Trino's built-in OpenMetrics endpoint scraped by Prometheus.

panels.title: Coordinator
panels.description: Prometheus scrape of the coordinator metrics endpoint.

panels.title: Active nodes
panels.description: Nodes (coordinator + workers) the coordinator currently sees as active.

panels.title: Inactive nodes
panels.description: Nodes that stopped announcing themselves (e.g. worker restart). Should be 0.

panels.title: Running queries
panels.description: Queries currently executing on the cluster.

panels.title: Queued queries
panels.description: Queries waiting for admission (resource groups / cluster capacity).

panels.title: Blocked queries
panels.description: Running queries whose every driver is blocked (waiting on memory, exchange or the connector).

panels.title: Queries / min
panels.description: Completed queries per minute (successful and failed).

panels.title: Failed / h
panels.description: Queries that failed in the last hour (all failure types).

panels.title: Failure rate
panels.description: Failed / completed over the rate interval.

panels.title: Execution p50 (5 min)
panels.description: Median query execution time (Trino's own 5-minute sliding window, from query start to end).

panels.title: Execution p99 (5 min)
panels.description: 99th percentile query execution time over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Cluster memory used
panels.description: Total query memory reservation / cluster query memory (sum of the general pools).

panels.title: Queries by state
panels.description: Gauges from the coordinator's QueryManager. Progressing = running queries that are making progress; fully blocked = all drivers blocked.

panels.title: Query outcomes / min
panels.description: Completed queries per minute split by outcome. Abandoned = the client stopped fetching results.

panels.title: Failures by type / h
panels.description: User error = bad SQL / missing table / permission; internal = Trino bug or node loss; external = the connector or underlying system failed; insufficient resources = memory/queue limits.

panels.title: Execution time percentiles (5-min window)
panels.description: Trino's own sliding 5-minute distribution of query execution time (start of execution to end, excluding queueing). Slow planning/analysis is included here.

panels.title: Queued time percentiles (5-min window)
panels.description: How long queries wait before they start executing. Grows when the cluster is saturated or resource groups throttle.

panels.title: Drivers
panels.description: Drivers are the pipeline instances executing splits. Many blocked drivers with few running ones point to a slow source (e.g. PostgreSQL) or memory pressure.

panels.title: Input rows / s
panels.description: Rows read from all connectors, cluster-wide.

panels.title: Input bytes / s
panels.description: Bytes read from all connectors, cluster-wide.

panels.title: CPU time consumed / s
panels.description: CPU seconds spent by queries per wall-clock second (= average cores busy with query work).

panels.title: Query duration seen by SCMP API (client side)
panels.description: End-to-end latency of Trino queries as measured by the SmartCity Management API (including HTTP round trips and result fetching). Independent of this dashboard's variables.

panels.title: Query duration seen by SCMP API: errors / min
panels.description: Trino calls from the SCMP API that ended in an error.

panels.title: Average time per phase (from query TIMELINE logs)
panels.description: Trino logs one TIMELINE line per finished query. This is the average of each phase over the interval. Planning = analysis + planning (includes connector metadata calls, e.g. JDBC table handles); waiting = time until the first task runs; scheduling = split scheduling; running = actual execution; finishing = result delivery.

targets.expr: avg_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | unwrap duration_seconds(planning) [$__auto]) by (app)

avg_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | unwrap duration_seconds(waiting) [$__auto]) by (app)

avg_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | unwrap duration_seconds(scheduling) [$__auto]) by (app)

avg_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | unwrap duration_seconds(running) [$__auto]) by (app)

avg_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | unwrap duration_seconds(finishing) [$__auto]) by (app)

panels.title: Elapsed time percentiles (from TIMELINE logs)
panels.description: Wall-clock time per query (begin to end) computed from the logs. Unlike the Prometheus percentiles this covers every query in the interval, not a sliding window.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.5, {namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | unwrap duration_seconds(elapsed) [$__auto]) by (app)

quantile_over_time(0.95, {namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | unwrap duration_seconds(elapsed) [$__auto]) by (app)

max_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | unwrap duration_seconds(elapsed) [$__auto]) by (app)

panels.title: Finished queries by state / interval
panels.description: FINISHED vs FAILED from the TIMELINE lines.

targets.expr: sum by (state) (count_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Failed queries by error code / interval
panels.description: Trino error codes of failed queries, e.g. ICEBERG_INVALID_METADATA, TABLE_NOT_FOUND, EXCEEDED_MEMORY_LIMIT.

targets.expr: sum by (error) (count_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} |= "TIMELINE" | regexp `TIMELINE: Query (?P<query_id>\S+) :: (?P<state>[A-Z]+)(?: \((?P<error>[A-Z_]+)\))? :: elapsed (?P<elapsed>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: planning (?P<planning>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: waiting (?P<waiting>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: scheduling (?P<scheduling>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: running (?P<running>[0-9.]+[a-z]+) :: finishing (?P<finishing>[0-9.]+[a-z]+)` | error != "" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Slow queries (elapsed ≥ 1 s) and failures
panels.description: TIMELINE lines of queries that took at least one second or failed. The query id can be looked up in the Trino Web UI or in the table below.

panels.title: Queries in coordinator memory
panels.description: system.runtime.queries keeps the last few hundred queries in the coordinator's memory (query.max-history). It is reset on restart.

panels.title: Cluster nodes
panels.description: Active nodes as reported by system.runtime.nodes.

targets.rawSQL: SELECT count(*) AS "Nodes", sum(CASE WHEN coordinator THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS "Workers" FROM system.runtime.nodes WHERE state = 'active'

panels.title: Average time per phase by client (ms)
panels.description: Where the time goes per client (source header of the connection), averaged over the queries still in coordinator memory. Execution = total minus queued, analysis and planning.

targets.rawSQL:
SELECT coalesce(source, '?') AS "Source",
       count(*) AS "Queries",
       sum(CASE WHEN state = 'FAILED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Failed",
       round(avg(queued_time_ms)) AS "Queued",
       round(avg(analysis_time_ms)) AS "Analysis",
       round(avg(planning_time_ms)) AS "Planning",
       round(avg(date_diff('millisecond', created, "end") - queued_time_ms - analysis_time_ms - planning_time_ms)) AS "Execution",
       round(avg(date_diff('millisecond', created, "end"))) AS "Total",
       max(date_diff('millisecond', created, "end")) AS "Max"
FROM system.runtime.queries
WHERE $__timeFilter(created) AND "end" IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Recent queries (system.runtime.queries)
panels.description: The coordinator's in-memory query history in the dashboard time range. Analysis = semantic analysis incl. connector metadata (table handles, columns, statistics); planning = optimizer; elapsed = created → end. Times in ms.

targets.rawSQL:
SELECT created AS "Created", state AS "State", coalesce(source, '?') AS "Source", "user" AS "User",
       queued_time_ms AS "Queued", analysis_time_ms AS "Analysis", planning_time_ms AS "Planning",
       date_diff('millisecond', created, coalesce("end", now())) AS "Elapsed",
       error_code AS "Error", query_id AS "Query ID", substr(regexp_replace(query, '\s+', ' '), 1, 160) AS "Query"
FROM system.runtime.queries
WHERE $__timeFilter(created)
ORDER BY created DESC
LIMIT 300

panels.title: Per client (system.runtime.queries)
panels.description: Aggregated by the client's source header. Times in ms.

targets.rawSQL:
SELECT coalesce(source, '?') AS "Source",
       count(*) AS "Queries",
       sum(CASE WHEN state = 'FAILED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Failed",
       round(avg(queued_time_ms)) AS "Queued",
       round(avg(analysis_time_ms)) AS "Analysis",
       round(avg(planning_time_ms)) AS "Planning",
       round(avg(date_diff('millisecond', created, "end") - queued_time_ms - analysis_time_ms - planning_time_ms)) AS "Execution",
       round(avg(date_diff('millisecond', created, "end"))) AS "Total",
       max(date_diff('millisecond', created, "end")) AS "Max"
FROM system.runtime.queries
WHERE $__timeFilter(created) AND "end" IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Nodes (system.runtime.nodes)
panels.description: Cluster membership as seen by the coordinator.

targets.rawSQL:
SELECT regexp_extract(http_uri, '//([^.]+)', 1) AS "Node", CASE WHEN coordinator THEN 'coordinator' ELSE 'worker' END AS "Role",
       state AS "State", node_version AS "Version", http_uri AS "URI"
FROM system.runtime.nodes ORDER BY 2, 1

panels.title: Nodes
panels.description: Node states from the coordinator's node manager. Queries wait while fewer than the required workers are active.

panels.title: Cluster memory
panels.description: Query memory available across all general pools vs. what running queries have reserved. Total includes revocable (spillable) memory.

panels.title: General memory pool per node
panels.description: Per-node general pool: reserved by tasks vs. pool size (query.max-memory-per-node). Reaching max blocks queries or kills them.

panels.title: Memory pool usage per node
panels.description: Reserved / max of the general pool per node.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (trino_memory_memorypool_reservedbytes{namespace="$namespace", job=~"$cluster-(coordinator|worker)-.*", pod=~"$pod", name="general"}) / max by (pod) (trino_memory_memorypool_maxbytes{namespace="$namespace", job=~"$cluster-(coordinator|worker)-.*", pod=~"$pod", name="general"})

panels.title: Distributed pool
panels.description: Cluster-wide view of the general pool as tracked by the coordinator.

panels.title: Memory incidents
panels.description: Kill counters are cumulative since coordinator start. Blocked nodes = nodes whose pool is exhausted. Spill only happens if spilling is enabled.

panels.title: Running splits per node
panels.description: Splits currently executing on each node's task executor.

panels.title: Pending leaf splits per node
panels.description: Source splits waiting for a thread. A growing backlog means the node is CPU-bound or the connector is slow.

panels.title: Tasks per node
panels.description: Tasks on the task executor vs. tasks tracked by the SqlTaskManager (includes finished tasks not yet cleaned up).

panels.title: Task executor threads per node
panels.description: Active threads vs. pool size (task.max-worker-threads). Queued > 0 with active = pool size means the node is saturated.

panels.title: Tasks created / failed per min
panels.description: Task churn per node. Failed tasks are retried or fail the query.

panels.title: Task input / output per node
panels.description: Bytes flowing into and out of tasks on each node (source reads + exchanges).

panels.title: Remote task round trips (coordinator → workers)
panels.description: Average HTTP round trip of the coordinator's task status/update/info requests to the workers. Spikes indicate network or worker GC problems.

panels.title: Remote task requests
panels.description: Coordinator → worker task requests. Failures happen when a worker is unreachable (restart, network).

panels.title: JDBC connections opened / s
panels.description: New JDBC connections to the PostgreSQL catalogs per second, by catalog and role. Trino opens a connection per split on the workers and per metadata call on the coordinator; there is no pooling by default.

panels.title: JDBC connection open latency p99 (5 min)
panels.description: How long opening a JDBC connection takes. High values point at the PostgreSQL pooler or network.

panels.title: JDBC failures / h
panels.description: Failed JDBC operations per hour by operation (openconnection, execute, getsplits, …) and catalog. Only operations with failures are shown.

targets.expr: sum by (op, name) (rate(label_replace({__name__=~"io_trino_plugin_jdbc_(jdbcclient|connectionfactory)_[a-z]+_failures_totalcount", namespace="$namespace", job=~"$cluster-(coordinator|worker)-.*", name=~"$catalog"}, "op", "$1", "__name__", "io_trino_plugin_jdbc_(?:jdbcclient|connectionfactory)_([a-z]+)_failures_totalcount")[$__rate_interval:1m]) * 3600) > 0

panels.title: Metadata operation latency p99 (5 min, coordinator)
panels.description: Connector calls made while analysing and planning a query: table handle, columns, statistics, splits, prepare. These are the JDBC round trips that make up Trino's analysis/planning time for PostgreSQL tables. Cached results (see cache hit rates) do not appear here.

panels.title: Metadata operations / s (coordinator)
panels.description: Rate of the same connector calls (cache misses only).

panels.title: Split read latency p99 (5 min, workers)
panels.description: Per-split work on the workers: get a connection, build the pushed-down SQL, abort/close the read connection. The actual PostgreSQL execution time is inside getconnectionwithsplit + the result iteration and is not measured separately.

panels.title: Split reads / s (workers)
panels.description: Rate of split-level JDBC operations.

panels.title: Coordinator metadata cache hit rate
panels.description: Hit rate of the CachingJdbcClient (metadata.cache-ttl). Low hit rates mean every query pays the metadata round trips to PostgreSQL again.

panels.title: Coordinator metadata cache requests / s
panels.description: Lookups against the metadata caches.

panels.title: JVM heap per pod
panels.description: Heap used vs. -Xmx. Trino's query memory pool lives inside the heap.

panels.title: GC time per pod
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time spent in garbage collection, by collector. Sustained values above a few percent slow every query; full GCs (Old Generation / MarkSweepCompact) stall the node.

panels.title: GC pauses / min per pod
panels.description: Number of collections per minute, by collector.

panels.title: CPU per pod
panels.description: CPU cores used by the trino container vs. its Kubernetes limit.

panels.title: CPU throttling per pod
panels.description: Share of CFS periods in which the container was throttled because it hit its CPU limit. Anything above ~10 % directly slows queries.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container="trino"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container="trino"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Container memory per pod
panels.description: Working set of the trino container vs. its memory limit. Hitting the limit means an OOM kill of the whole JVM.

panels.title: Threads per pod
panels.description: Live JVM threads.

panels.title: Open file descriptors per pod
panels.description: Sockets and files. Each JDBC connection and each exchange buffer uses descriptors.

panels.title: Container restarts
panels.description: Cumulative restarts of the trino container. A restart drops all running queries on that node and empties the coordinator's query history.

panels.title: Log lines by level
panels.description: Trino's log format is `timestamp<TAB>LEVEL<TAB>thread<TAB>logger<TAB>message`.

panels.title: Warnings and errors by logger
panels.description: Which component produces warnings and errors, e.g. io.trino.node.RemoteNodeState when a worker is unreachable.

targets.expr: sum by (logger) (count_over_time({namespace="$namespace", app="trino", pod=~"$pod"} | regexp `^\S+\t(?P<level>WARN|ERROR)\t\S+\t(?P<logger>\S+)\t` | level != "" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Warnings and errors
panels.description: All WARN and ERROR lines of the selected pods.
